articles.title: South Africa Already Upgraded by Bond Market as Rating Firms Lag
articles.summary: South African authorities are focused on hitting budget targets rather than pleasing credit-rating firms, according to the government’s top finance official — and the reward is a bond market that’s already pricing the country’s debt as investment grade.

articles.title: Goldman Skeptical of Dollar-Dominance Threats After Yen Support
articles.summary: US support for Japan’s efforts to prop up the yen is unlikely to damage the dollar’s status as the most dominant reserve currency in the world, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

articles.title: Zimbabwe’s VFEX Plans $5 Billion Market Value, Venture Board for Mining
articles.summary: Zimbabwe’s dollar-denominated stock exchange plans to increase its market value by 25% over the next year as it rolls out new products, including a venture board to help junior mining and exploration companies raise capital.

articles.title: Iran Wants to Bar US, Israeli Ships From Hormuz in Deal
articles.summary: Iran will seek to bar US and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and require compensation from hostile countries before they’re allowed to sail through it, according to local media reports on a proposed Iran-Oman deal. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Asia Pacific Share Sales Overcome Volatility to Shatter Records
articles.summary: Blockbuster share sales from artificial intelligence-related companies in the Asia Pacific led to a record for equity capital markets activity last month, despite weakness in the region’s stock markets.

articles.title: UK IPO Slump Hurting Private Equity and Venture, PitchBook Says
articles.summary: The UK’s sluggish market for initial public offering is leaving private equity and venture capital firms with fewer exit routes, increasing their reliance on sales to other buyout shops or large corporates for returns, PitchBook data show.

articles.title: Pacific Basin CEO Says Industry Faces Shift After Iran Conflict

articles.title: Trading Strategies ‘Buried Alive’ by India’s Rocky Stock Reform
articles.summary: For much of the first week of trading under India’s new auction system to set closing stock prices, traders were convinced that one of the most consequential market structure reforms in years was faltering.

articles.title: Hong Kong's Iconic Diners Go Global
articles.summary: Hong Kong has exported everything from cinema to finance. Now, its iconic cha chaan teng diners are going global too. Mary Hui explains how these humble cafes have become a symbol of culture, migration and identity. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Copper Heads for Record Close in London on Tighter Global Market
articles.summary: Copper headed for a record close in London after strong gains fueled by signs of tighter supply across the global market.

articles.title: Japan Confirms Three-Day Yen Intervention in Spring to Lift Yen
articles.summary: Japan said it intervened in the currency market three times during the spring Golden Week holiday to prop up the yen, going beyond its recent twin-punch playbook with an additional round in an apparent effort to maximize the psychological impact on investors.

articles.title: Taiwan Pension Fund Will Tap Third-Party Managers for Stock Bets
articles.summary: Taiwan’s $49 billion public-sector pension fund is planning to allocate more assets to third-party managers to boost its exposure to global stock markets.

articles.title: Why the Yen Is Surrendering Intervention Gains
articles.summary: The yen is heading into the end of the week having surrendered nearly half of its intervention-driven gains, fueling speculation among traders that authorities may step into the market again. Bloomberg's David Finnerty breaks down how traders see recent FX moves. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SpaceX Shares Climb After $100 Billion Insider Lockup Expires
